evals.prompt: I need a treasury account that requires 2 of 3 approvers to release funds. Set it up so any two of three specific keys can authorize a transfer, then schedule a 500 HBAR payout from that treasury that only executes once two of the three have signed. Use @hiero-ledger/sdk.
evals.expected_output: A complete script that creates a 2-of-3 threshold KeyList, creates an account owned by it, and schedules a transfer requiring two of the three signatures before it executes.
assertions: The output constructs a KeyList with an explicit threshold argument, not KeyList.of(...) which requires every key
The KeyList threshold is set to 2, matching the 2-of-3 requirement
The output creates a real account owned by the threshold key
The KeyList is built from .publicKey values, not raw PrivateKey objects — passing private keys into a KeyList is a real, silent bug this skill documents
The output includes ScheduleCreateTransaction: Wraps the transfer in a schedule instead of executing it directly
The output includes setScheduledTransaction: Attaches the actual TransferTransaction to the schedule

evals.prompt: After creating a scheduled transaction, write the code to check whether it has executed yet and log the result. Use @hiero-ledger/sdk and ScheduleInfoQuery.
evals.expected_output: Code that queries ScheduleInfo and correctly checks execution status, aware that the executed field is nullable rather than boolean.
assertions: The output uses ScheduleInfoQuery to check status

The output checks `.executed` truthiness (e.g. `if (info.executed)`) or compares explicitly against null — never `.executed === true`, since ScheduleInfo.executed is null-or-Timestamp, never a literal boolean, and that comparison silently never matches even after real execution

evals.prompt: Schedule a payment that should be cancellable by the treasury admin if it's not approved within a week, and make sure it doesn't just silently disappear if nobody signs in time. Use @hiero-ledger/sdk.
evals.expected_output: A schedule created with an admin key (so it can be explicitly deleted) and either an appropriate expirationTime or waitForExpiry(true) so the pending approval isn't lost to a default expiration.
assertions: The output sets an admin key so the schedule can be explicitly deleted/cancelled

The output either sets an explicit expirationTime for the one-week window, or sets waitForExpiry(true) so a slow-to-sign schedule isn't deleted early — addressing the 'expiration is real, not just documentation' pitfall this skill documents
